parsed.explanation: No traveller-facing state restriction is documented: no criminalisation of expression, no facility or ward exclusion, no border document friction, no police targeting of trans people; legal protections are strong and courts have recognised hate motive and convicted attackers. The negatives are societal, not institutional: equality bodies report rising violence and intimidation with trans people especially affected, a recurring dating-app ambush pattern (robbery, humiliation, assault) that police record and prosecute but which many victims leave unreported, and high harassment prevalence (a dated 2019 LGBT-wide regional figure, given limited weight). The hate-crime statute lacks definition and a recording code, so recourse runs through general provisions — a real but partial gap, not absent. Functioning prosecution and no universal exposure keep this in Reduced Risk; documented violence above background holds it below the 0.75 tier.
